chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'shah) from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Basir who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man hunted a gazelle while he was in the state of Ihram, and he broke its arm or leg, so the gazelle went about on its face, and he did not know what he had done. He said: 'Upon him is its ransom.' I said: 'Indeed, he saw it afterwards walking.' He said: 'Upon him is a quarter of its price.'

And it is not permissible for anyone to hunt while he is facing the Sanctuary (Mecca), even if he is Muhtal (not in Ihram). If he hunts it and kills it, its meat is forbidden, and upon him is the ransom. Narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فِدَاء: Ransom or compensation for a religious obligation or violation
key_terms.مُحِلّ: One who is not in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ransom for accidentally wounding a hunted animal while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam, transmitted through the chain of Abu Basir, elucidates the proportional liability for wounding versus killing game, reflecting the juristic principle that compensation scales with the extent of the loss. It further extends the prohibition to non-pilgrims hunting within the Haram boundaries, a point of scholarly discussion regarding the spatial scope of the sanctity. The ruling underscores the continuity of the 'Haram' status for the animal's meat even after the hunter's Ihram ends, provided the kill occurred within the sacred precincts.
